newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA WARY OF PAY-PER-VIEW REVOLUTION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA WARY OF PAY-PER-VIEW REVOLUTION.

text.p: World Cup soccer matches and those in the European Championship and Olympic Games must remain on public access TV and free of charge to as many people as possible, UEFA said on Friday.

Gerhard Aigner, the General Secretary of European soccer's ruling body, said that Friday's Executive Committee meeting had fully supported the stance taken by the International Olympic Committee and FIFA, world soccer's governing body, in protecting those major events for public access television.
UEFA have not ruled out pay-per-view television screening matches in the major tournaments, but said that access on pay TV must be controlled and limited.
Aigner said: "We believe these events must be seen in as many countries as possible. Major event live football must be protected and our principle is that we want to show the big matches to everyone.
"However, we do not deny that pay TV should have some access to the major events, but we believe that if it does it should only be on a limited scale.

"For example, when the World Cup is in Asia in 2002 and some matches are being shown live at one o'clock in the morning in Europe when there may not be a huge public demand to watch it, would there be anything wrong in showing that match on pay TV. This is something we would have to think about."

The input of huge amounts of money from satelite TV companies across Europe like BSkyB and Canal Plus have helped to bring about a revolution in soccer in recent years and the advent of more pay-per-view TV is immanent according to many commentators.

UEFA'S stance is that a balance has to be maintained. "The subject is becoming more important because of pay-per-view coming in," said Aigner, and there are possibly ways of utilising it for a limited or a minority audience makes sense.

The Executive Committee only discussed the three international tournaments and did not discuss the impact that pay-per-view may have in the future on club competitions like the European Champions' league or domestic championships.
